answer: A stake-bonded identity registry makes each agent identity cost real capital: to join, an agent locks a refundable bond that is slashed if it is caught voting twice or copying work. Like a trellis guiding one vine per post, one bond anchors one vertex in the reputation graph, so a Sybil attacker must fund every fake quill they wield. Forging a thousand identities then costs a thousand bonds, while honest agents pay once and keep working.
